findings.text: follow-on: the partial full-machine probe's header line declares `rev dcfbaed2a` (the base revision) while its body prints head-only keys (`contact_rz_m`, `nearest_node_index`), so the log's declared revision does not match the code it exercised; the probe is explicitly superseded by logs/benchmark_contact_lookup.log, whose header correctly names head 0923d9782, so the benchmark evidence is bound elsewhere and this is a record-hygiene note rather than an unbound claim.

follow-on: the committed receipt still carries the pre-change keys `tangency_node_index` and `angle_formula_index_hits_pi` that `_limiter_node_construction` no longer emits, so a reader consulting it reads a contact read the benchmark has abandoned; it lives under a different plan's figure directory and outside this node's grant, and the manifest lists it honestly as follow-on (a).

follow-on: the base arm of the suite ran from a scratch extraction under /tmp/reckon-crew-scratch/r-20261006T043403884339-cfs-limiter-designed-contact/base-tree (its module_under_test names that path), not from one shared tree, so base and head arms differ in import path and working directory; the summary counts match (9/10/3 passed against 9/10/3 passed) with no deselection on either arm, so the delta is zero and the mismatch is a provenance note, not a selectable-difference risk of the kind a missing root conftest produces.

item_verdicts.call_sites: three consumers, all in the node's declared paths: the test's `_designed_tangency` helper, `limiter_read_resolution_audit._limiter_node_construction`, and `wall_at_cell_pitch._wall_metrics`; a git grep of tests/, benchmarks/ and scripts/ at head finds no remaining `(n-1)//2`/`(wall_nodes-1)//2` contact reader and no consumer of the removed `tangency_node_index`/`node_flux_wb`/`angle_formula_index_hits_pi` keys.
item_verdicts.diff: read at head 0923d9782 by inspection and against base dcfbaed2a: the single commit adds `designed_contact` to scripts/analytic_oracle_fixtures/measure.py, points all three consumers at it, replaces the 241-to-481 convergence assertion with `test_weak_contact_position_is_exact_at_both_wall_resolutions` on `CONTACT_ROUNDOFF_BOUND_M = 1e-9`, and adds the evidence fragment; git diff --stat touches exactly the five declared paths, 94 insertions and 59 deletions.
item_verdicts.done_when: the five clauses are met: measure.py exposes `designed_contact(wall)` documented with its construction; the test helper and both benchmarks delegate to it and the repeat grep finds no other index reader; the second-order assertion is replaced by the exact-by-construction bound with a docstring that says so; the three gate modules record 9/10/3 passed at head equal to 9/10/3 at base (added failures 0) and the 121-node benchmark contact reads R = 7.80139579 m; the negative control reddens the contact assertions.
item_verdicts.goal_fidelity: the node goal is one owner for the analytic limiter's designed contact that every test and benchmark reads; the diff gives `scripts/analytic_oracle_fixtures/measure.py:236` that owner and routes the test helper and both benchmark contact readers through it, with no consumer left reading a vertex index.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records status complete, the one commit 0923d9782, the three gate arms with their logs, the negative control with its red log, the R = 7.80139579 m contact for the weak wall at every sampled count, and the stale-receipt follow-on.
item_verdicts.reuse: the node is itself a consolidation: it deletes the duplicated `_designed_tangency` body from the test and routes test and both benchmarks through the one fixture function, removing the pre-existing duplication the rebaseline review recorded.
item_verdicts.write_paths: git diff dcfbaed2a..0923d9782 touches exactly scripts/analytic_oracle_fixtures/measure.py, tests/test_topology_limiter_contact.py, benchmarks/limiter_read_resolution_audit.py, benchmarks/wall_at_cell_pitch.py and the fragment, every one inside the declared scope and nothing else; the reviewed worktree is clean.

justifications.durability: the new assertion compares the topology solver's read contact (`read.wall_point`, derived from the flux state) against a reference derived independently from the wall polygon geometry, so it is not self-referential, and the negative control demonstrates it is sensitive: restoring the old `(len(wall)-1)//2` index against the repaired wall reddens `test_limiter_contact_is_spline_authored_at_analytic_tangency` and `test_weak_contact_position_is_exact_at_both_wall_resolutions` (2 failed, 7 passed, EXIT=1); the bound replaces a convergence claim the operating point cannot exercise, so the test now states the strongest contract the geometry supports.
justifications.evidence: the six gate logs carry proper headers (revision, module_under_test, cwd, literal command), the after arm names head 0923d9782 and the base arm names dcfbaed2a with its scratch tree; the negative control is red with two failing ids the head arm does not fail; I independently reproduced `tests/test_topology_limiter_contact.py` at head with 9 passed, EXIT=0; the benchmark probes show contact_R=7.80139579 for the weak wall at 121/241/481/961 nodes and panel 120 of 121 selected. Weakened by the superseded probe log's base-revision header, the stale committed receipt, and the base arm's scratch-tree provenance.
justifications.fit: `designed_contact` is a small public function placed beside `limiter_contour` in the fixture module, follows the module's array-in/array-out idiom, and the test helper becomes a one-line delegation; comments are rewritten to state the mechanism (exact by construction, flux rounding along the stationary edge) rather than the discarded convergence claim, with no plan, stage or ticket label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: all five done-when clauses verified at head 0923d9782: the owner exists and is documented, the test and both benchmarks delegate to it, the repeat grep finds no other index-based contact reader, the second-order assertion is replaced by the exact-by-construction bound with a truthful docstring, the gate is green at 9/10/3 against base 9/10/3, and the negative control reddens the new assertion.
justifications.reuse: the change removes a duplicated construction (the test's own `_designed_tangency` body) and installs a single owner that the test and both benchmarks share, which is the node's whole purpose and the fix for the divergence the rebaseline review recorded; `_limiter_node_construction` still computes its nearest node by an argmin of its own, but that is a distinct query, not a re-implementation of the contact.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff dcfbaed2a..0923d9782 touches exactly the five declared paths and nothing else; the reviewed worktree is clean; the only stale artifact found (the cut-cell-current-attribution receipt) lies outside the grant and is reported as a follow-on rather than edited.
